intervals.label: collaboration active
intervals.note: Day precision, from the collaboration's own paper. Mass 240 t at the start, 912 t from June 1985. The quote is three consecutive sentences of that section.
intervals.quote: Continuous data taking started February 19, 1984 with a mass of 240 tons. The size of the detector was gradually increased until the final mass of 912 tons was reached in June 1985. Data taking ended September 13, 1988.

intervals.label: collaboration completed
intervals.note: Terminal event copied from the experiment record: end of data taking, not a dissolution date.

name: Fréjus Collaboration
notes: Institutions on the 1991 paper: RWTH Aachen (1. Physikalisches Institut), LAL Orsay, LPNHE Ecole Polytechnique Palaiseau, DPhPE CEN-Saclay, Bergische Universität-Gesamthochschule Wuppertal. No official institution count or roster was found.

summary.plain: The group of German and French physicists from Aachen, Orsay, Palaiseau, Saclay and Wuppertal who built and ran the Fréjus detector.
summary.technical: Collaboration operating the Fréjus nucleon-decay detector at the Laboratoire Souterrain de Modane.
